_README: Editable file with monthly Highlights & Lowlights for DAE dashboard.
Edit this file when a new month closes. Save it in the same folder as make_executive_summary.py.
When you run `python make_executive_summary.py`, it reads this file and updates the dashboard.
pnl_notes:  optional extra notes per P&L line (Revenue commentary is auto-generated from Excel data).
HTML allowed in body for formatting:
Months use format Mmm-YY (e.g., May-26, Jun-26). To add a new month, copy any existing block and change the key.
P&L Commentary is AUTO-GENERATED from your Excel using this framework:
Revenue: closed at $X (X% MoM; X% vs Bud) driven by Revenue per Hour, Supply Hours, Trips/Hour, Price/Trip, Active Drivers, Hires/Churn
Gross Profit: from Revenue + OPEX drivers (Driver Payments, Maintenance, Marketing, Uber Take Rate, etc.)
EBITDA: from GP + SG&A drivers (Direct Business Line, Cross Func + Corp G&A, Payroll)
Net Income: from EBITDA + D&A + Interest + Taxes
You only fill highlights/lowlights. P&L commentary updates automatically when Excel data changes.

_TEMPLATE_NEW_MONTH._comment: Copy this block, rename key to e.g. 'May-26', fill in highlights & lowlights.

highlights.title: LTO leasing to DAE
highlights.body: Transitioned the 45 cumulative vehicles from LTO to DAE, including 32 GAC AION ES and 13 BYD D1 units. We expect to continue transitioning additional LTO units ahead of the World Cup.

highlights.title: Uber-VEMO World Cup Initiative
highlights.body: A strategic agreement has been reached with Uber under which a revenue-per-hour guarantee will be applied to 30 vehicles positioned at a dedicated pickup point 300m from Estadio Azteca, ensuring VEMO Conduce vehicles serve outbound stadium traffic. Vehicles are required to be on-site 2 hours before each match. Uber will pay USD $2,500 per game for the 30-vehicle block. Accounting for 2 hours of transit and 2 hours of pre-game standby, the effective guarantee yields MXN $314/hr — 6% above our internal World Cup projection and 30% above December 2025 actuals.

highlights.title: VEMO World Cup Initiative
highlights.body:
We have planned a set of initiatives to increase the revenue performance of our business line during the World Cup.
• Jersey Raffle: 10 jerseys per hub raffled (every week) among drivers with perfect attendance and no sinister incidents; promotion runs two weeks before Mexico's inaugural game vs. South Africa through 3 days before Mexico's final group stage match.
• Attendance Grace Period: Pre-June 8th absences excluded from attendance tracking, enabling ~400 drivers to qualify for Gold category.
• Gold-Exclusive Objectives: Two new compensation objectives added — available only to Gold drivers during World Cup Season (June-July) — designed to drive revenue growth, reduce unattendance, and push more drivers into Band 4+.
• Demand Intelligence Calendar: High-demand cultural, festival, and sports events mapped for June-July, including all Fan Fest locations across Mexico City, to help drivers identify peak demand zones proactively.

lowlights.title: Performance Ratio
lowlights.body:
Decreased by -470 bps MoM (68.7% vs. 73.4%) and -922 bps vs. Budget (68.7% vs. 77.9%) and were -6.6% below Budget (243,738 vs. 260,866). The decrease in PR was mainly driven by:
• Hiring: closed +13.2% MoM in hires (513 vs. 453); despite the monthly increase, hires were concentrated at month-end and did not translate into a meaningful PR recovery.
  – Driving Test Filter: The filter, tightened in March to preserve fleet image, was reset to January-February levels to support PR recovery. The historical fail rate averaged 19% (Q4 2025-Feb 2026). Following the tightening, it averaged 40.5%, representing a net loss of 158 drivers in March and 211 in April. In the final two weeks of May, the fail rate came down to 25%, yielding a net headcount gain of 52 drivers by month-end.
  – Lead quality: May set another lead volume record at 14,400 (+55% vs. January, +102% vs. February). Despite this, total hires were -27% vs. January and -3.8% vs. February. Two factors explain the gap: (i) Hot sale CDMX: From May 25 to June 2, high-spending retail advertisers compressed available ad inventory, driving CPL up and conversion rates down; and (ii) Timing of initiatives: Both key initiatives — reducing driving test strictness from 40% to 25% and doubling the marketing budget from MXN $300K to MXN $600K/month — were launched in the second half of May only, limiting their impact on monthly results.

lowlights.title: Churn
lowlights.body:
Overall churn decreased from 34.4% to 31.9%, normalized for the transition of 40 DAE drivers to LTO.
• Bronze Category Drivers: Bronze drivers account for 51% of total churn; Bronze Beginner adds another 25%, for a combined 76%. Silver and Silver Beginner represent 12%; Gold and Gold Beginner only 4%. Bronze remains the primary retention focus, as these drivers do not yet meet VEMO Conduce performance standards.
• Increase in churn of new drivers: Churn among drivers with 0-30 days of tenure increased 11%, consistent with the reduction in driving test stringency — lower entry filters produce less-qualified driver profiles and higher early drop-off rates.

highlights.title: LTO leasing to DAE
highlights.body: Transitioned the 54 cumulative vehicles from LTO to DAE, including 36 GAC AION ES and 18 BYD D1 units, reflecting an accelerating pace of repossessed-vehicle absorption into active operations. The program converts otherwise idle inventory, previously incurring sunk parking and insurance costs — in addition to losses when either leased again or auctioned — into revenue-generating DAE assets, with continued transitions expected as additional LTO repossessions become available.

highlights.title: VEMO World Cup Initiative
highlights.body: Successfully executed all 5 World Cup matches held in Mexico City, deploying a 30-vehicle DAE block to Uber's dedicated pickup point at Estadio Azteca for each game. Uber paid US$2,500 per game for the block, equivalent to an effective MXN $314/hr, consistent with the guarantee negotiated ahead of the tournament, and Uber was very pleased with the execution, which ended up generating MXN $237,117. Separately, secured a co-branding agreement covering full vehicle wraps on 5 units at MXN $2,500/unit, a 67% premium over our standard co-branding rate of MXN $1,500.

highlights.title: Charger Relocation Proposal
highlights.body: Evaluating the consolidation of 8 charging units from Artz into San Pedro hub. Artz has structurally underperformed on nightshift fill rate due to limited public transport access in the area, driving persistent driver leakage; San Pedro has already demonstrated stronger fill-rate performance under comparable conditions. Consolidating into a single, larger hub is expected to generate economies of scale, reduce headcount requirements, and improve DAE-wide Performance Ratio by reducing hub-driven attrition. Evaluating potential impact of converting Artz into a RHF site given otherwise onerous cancellation penalties.

highlights.title: Samsara
highlights.body: Completed full Samsara deployment across the fleet, confirming strong performance in event-detection accuracy. As a direct result, reported accident-rate metrics have increased, reflecting more precise incident capture rather than a deterioration in driving behavior. Work is underway to incorporate the Samsara Driver Safety Score into the compensation framework, aligning driver incentives with safety performance and targeting a reduction in at-fault incidents over time.

highlights.title: Corporate SG&A Reallocation
highlights.body: Corporate and cross-functional cost allocation across business lines was rebalanced to reflect actual time and resource demands versus budget. VCN's share rose from 30% to 32%, DAE's from 15% to 20%, with LTO absorbing the corresponding reduction, driven by DAE's larger fleet and LTO's smaller active portfolio.

lowlights.title: Performance Ratio
lowlights.body:
Improved +170 bps MoM (70.4% vs. 68.7%) though -756 bps vs. Budget (70.4% vs. 78.0%). Supply hours increased +2.7% MoM (250,317 vs. 243,738) and were +0.1% above Budget (250,317 vs. 250,067). The decrease in PR vs Budget was mainly driven by:
• Hiring: closed +42.3% MoM in hires (730 vs. 513); the increase was mainly driven by:
  – Lead quality: Another record month in lead generation, reaching 16,893 leads in June (+17.3% MoM vs. 14,400 in May). Despite record hires, conversion of hire from same-month leads held flat at 1.3% — the same rate as May, against the 2.5% seen in January and February. This confirms the constraint is conversion efficiency, not lead volume: we are generating more leads than we can convert. July's target is to sustain June's lead volume while recovering to Jan/Feb conversion rates of ca. 2.5%.

lowlights.title: Churn
lowlights.body: Overall churn increased from 31.9% to 33.6%, normalized for the transition of 41 DAE drivers to LTO. The increase was mainly driven by higher churn among new drivers, which is consistent with record hiring months and the entry of a larger low-tenure driver cohort.

lowlights.title: Uber Rebate
lowlights.body: The Uber Rebate for DAE ran from Q1'24 through Q1'26, applying a 7.5% take rate to 450 vehicles of the VEMO fleet, subject to LTO's credit allocation (7.5%/450 held at 100% LTO attainment vs. Uber target). In Q2'26, covered fleet dropped from 450 to 300 vehicles, mechanically pushing the implied take rate to 9% on its own; LTO then reached only 78% of its quarterly allocation target, compounding the rate to an implied 11.4% for the quarter, a MXN $4.8m OPEX impact vs. Q1'26. Budget had assumed renegotiation back to 7.5%/450 terms for Q2'26; that didn't happen, meaning the OPEX offset vs. budget applies from Q2'26 onward, not as a one-time hit. Absent renegotiation, the structure continues to erode: Q3'26 fleet drops to 150 vehicles (implied take rate 14%), and Q4'26 reverts to the pre-2024 baseline of 15%.

lowlights.title: World Cup Marketplace
lowlights.body: Demand uplift fell short of Uber's forecast, in line with a market-wide miss. Uber projected marketplace growth vs. December '25 of +5% for June and +3% for July; actuals came in below that benchmark, with June RPH -7% vs. forecast and the first two weeks of July -9% vs. forecast. The shortfall mirrors the broader market: Deloitte reported the tournament's economic impact in Mexico landed 7% below its pre-tournament estimate, driven by lower international tourist inflows, shorter average stays, and consumption concentrated only on Mexico's match days, while road closures and mobility restrictions in host cities reduced foot traffic in certain areas. Despite the softer uplift, Ride Hailing Revenue reached +22.5% vs. budget, confirming the miss is against Uber's optimistic tournament scenario.

highlights.title: Revenue Performance
highlights.body:
Closed at MXN $57.4m (-2.1% MoM; +15.7% vs. Budget), mainly driven by:
• Revenue per Hour: -8.5% MoM (MXN $206.7 vs. MXN $225.8), and +9.4% vs. Budget (MXN $206.8 vs. MXN $189.0), on account of (i) a higher price per trip of MXN $143.4 (vs. MXN $132.5 Budget); and (ii) higher trips per hour of 1.44 (vs 1.43 Budget).

highlights.title: Monumento a la Madre & San Pedro Expansion
highlights.body: Evaluating the conversion of Monumento a la Madre from a DAE hub into a VCN ride-hailing operation. While Monumento a la Madre has performed well as a DAE hub, its highly central location and strong Uber revenue metrics make it attractive for VCN's ride-hailing model. In parallel, consolidating its 13 charging units into San Pedro would increase vehicle density at a single DAE hub, generating operating efficiencies and supporting improved DAE-wide Performance Ratio, while unlocking a strategic location for VCN in one of the city's most active ride-hailing corridors.

highlights.title: Samsara
highlights.body: Full Samsara deployment across the fleet was completed on July 13. Since deployment, responsible accidents declined 37% (from 62 (week of Jul 13) to 39 (week of Aug 3), and AARK responsible declined 39% (from 5.33 to 3.24). While the post-deployment period remains too short to establish a sustained trend, the early results are encouraging. The Samsara Driver Safety Score has also begun to be incorporated into driver compensation: during the first week of August, 45 drivers, representing 1.6% of the active fleet, were impacted in their compensation through their Samsara score, creating a direct link between safety performance and driver earnings.

highlights.title: Uber Airport Licensing Opportunity
highlights.body: In early-stage discussions with Uber to establish VEMO Conduce as a licensed operator for passenger pickup and drop-off within Mexico City airport federal zone. A key requirement is that all drivers hold a valid Federal License, issued through SICT-authorized training. We are advancing with CECAFED, a certified third-party provider, with an estimated certification cost of approximately $10,000 MXN per driver and current capacity of 15–30 drivers per week, primarily constrained by medical-exam processing capacity. The Category F license also requires 65 hours of training. In parallel, we are evaluating alternative certified providers to optimize both cost and driver throughput, as well as the feasibility of establishing an in-house SICT-authorized VEMO training center as a medium-term solution to reduce costs and increase capacity. The in-house alternative is estimated to require 6–8 months to implement. Uber is currently developing the economic model, and we are awaiting their formal proposal before advancing internal structuring discussions. Outside legal counsel review remains ongoing.

lowlights.title: Performance Ratio
lowlights.body: Improved +300 bps MoM (73.4% vs. 70.4%) though -456 bps vs. Budget (70.4% vs. 73.4%). Supply hours increased +8.1% MoM (270,527 vs. 250,317) and were +5.8% above Budget (270,527 vs. 255,412). The decrease in PR vs Budget was mainly driven by:

lowlights.title: Hiring
lowlights.body: Closed in line with June's hiring levels (726 vs. 730), marking the second-best month of the year. This was achieved with a leaner recruiting team (18 recruiters vs. 21 earlier in the year), supported by AI recruiting agent María, which is expected to enable a further reduction of 3 FTEs next month.

lowlights.title: Churn
lowlights.body:
Overall churn increased from 33.6% to 40.8%, normalized for the transition of 43 DAE drivers to LTO. The increase was mainly driven by higher churn among new drivers, which is consistent with record hiring months and the entry of a larger low-tenure driver cohort.
• The tenure indicates that July's deterioration was concentrated among new hires: the 15–30 day bucket hit 151 exits (+63 vs. YTD average, +40 vs. June) and 31–60 days hit 146 (+44 vs. average, +60 vs. June, the largest MoM increase of any group). These buckets are consistent with the unusually large low-tenure cohorts created during the June-July hiring ramp. By contrast, churn beyond 90 days remained broadly stable, confirming the deterioration was concentrated primarily among newer drivers.
• Continuous Absenteeism drove nearly half of all churn (345 exits, 49.7%), 124 above average and the clearest sign that a meaningful share of recent hires never did fully engage with operations. QHSE sanctions (106, +33) and resignations (90, +16) followed. Separately, 62 drivers exited before ever reaching operations (35 never completed a trip, 27 were absent on Day 2 of VEMO Uni), highlighting pre-operational attrition as an additional area of focus. — excluding those, the adjusted churn rate falls to ~39.6%.
